title: Seller Signal Cluster Playlets (draft)
content:
Summary:
This is a lightweight, seller-ready pack of tiny battlecards ("playlets") keyed to emergent customer signals. Aim: give SEs/AMs 60–90s micro-answers that map a runtime/business signal to a concrete Redwood narrative + demo prompt + quick fallback.

Why this exists (context):
- We see repetitive inbound and pilot patterns driven by short lists of deployment signals (cost-sensitivity spike, latency incident tolerance, security/regulatory gating).
- Long battlecards are great for training but not for live calls. We need ultra-short, clustered responses that map signal -> ask -> outcome -> next step.
- This doc is intentionally terse: it's a set of stubs to iterate with field feedback.

How to use:
- Pick a signal cluster (one-liner). Use the playlet script on discovery calls or Slack responses.
- Each playlet includes: 1) one-sentence customer claim, 2) 30s seller framing, 3) two supporting data points / proof lines, 4) a short demo prompt / artifact, 5) a fallback plan and pilot gating.

Signal clusters (short definitions):
1) Cost-Sprint: sudden emphasis on reducing per-token cost or previewing bill shock.
2) Latency-Anchor: product owner needs sub-100ms p50 for short chat flows or p99 < 500ms for low-latency features.
3) Data-Privacy-Lock: procurement requires VPC/air-gapped or strict KMS controls.
4) Scale-Burst: unpredictable traffic with large short spikes (marketing-driven events).
5) Quality-Slippage: accuracy/regression concern after model change or rollout.

Playlets (micro-battlecards):
---
Playlet: Cost-Sprint
Customer claim: "We need to reduce our inference spend by ~40% or pilots don't proceed."
30s framing: "We treat cost as a leaky pipe: small runtime levers compound. Redwood Optimize finds quick wins (batching / KV caching / quantization) and our Dedicated offers predictable unit costs for bursty flows.
"
Proof lines (2):
- Pilot case: fintech aggregator reduced token spend by 33% in 2 weeks via prefix caching + smaller model fallback for low-confidence steps (internal case GM-1987).
- Transparent cost dashboard: seller can demo token-level breakdown live and show per-route delta.

Demo prompt / asset: "Open Redwood Console > Route X > Cost breakdown. Show: token distribution per model, cache hit rate, and hypothetical impact of enabling 4-token prefix cache."
Fallback / pilot gating: start with hosted API pilot limited to a single customer route with preconfigured caching and automatic fallback to quantized family. Success metric: 30% cost reduction without >5% latency regressions.
Action ask: ask for sample traffic CSV and spike times for quick estimate.
---
Playlet: Latency-Anchor
Customer claim: "We need user-facing replies in <200ms (p50) or it’s unusable."
30s framing: "High-throughput runtime + compiled kernels -> we optimize for steady-state latency. For time-critical paths, we suggest short-context models, KV pre-warming, and Dedicated pools pinned to the route."
Proof lines (2):
- Internal benchmark: conversational path (<=64 tokens) reached p50 120ms on Dedicated with continuous batching disabled for that pool.
- Fallback policy: when p99 exceeds threshold, immediate routing to a lower-latency model variant.
Demo asset / script: show SLO page in Console: per-route p50/p99 graph, and drill into tracing for a single token span.
Fallback / pilot gating: configure canary with p50 target, and a circuit-breaker to switch to low-latency variant. Metric: <200ms p50 for 7-day window.
Action ask: capture typical sequence lengths and synchronous vs async UX requirements.
---
Playlet: Data-Privacy-Lock
Customer claim: "We can’t send any PII to a multi-tenant endpoint—need VPC or on-prem."
30s framing: "We offer Redwood Private with customer-managed CP and KMS/HSM options. For proof, we can run an early audit and provide a SOC-style evidence packet for the pilot."
Proof lines (2):
- Feature: customer VPC + private control plane, optional air-gapped on-prem bundle.
- Compliance: example SOC2/ISO references + audit checklist we can share within 48h.
Demo asset / script: link to the Private deployment checklist and sample network diagram.
Fallback / pilot gating: start with a scoped Dedicated pool in a customer VPC and escalate to full Private if audit passes.
Action ask: ask for regulatory authority name and specific data classification policy doc.
---
Playlet: Scale-Burst
Customer claim: "We have weekend campaign spikes 10x baseline and need predictable capacity."
30s framing: "Reserved Dedicated capacity + autoscaling with burst allowances plus routing policies get you predictable capacity during events."
Proof lines (2):
- Case: commerce customer used reserved pool + burst buffer to survive Black Friday promo without degradation.
- Mechanic: autoscaler with warm-worker buffer plus pre-warmed KV cache reduces cold-start tail.
Demo asset / script: show capacity planner sheet (simple table) and how burst policy affects cost.
Fallback / pilot gating: provision minimal reserved pool and a burst window; success = no dropped requests during synthetic spike test.
Action ask: get expected qps curve and marketing calendar.
---
Playlet: Quality-Slippage
Customer claim: "After a model upgrade our results look worse on active prompts."
30s framing: "Rollouts + eval hooks are designed for exactly this. Redwood Optimize can run diff-evals on your prompt set and we can pin old model while we investigate."
Proof lines (2):
- Feature: rollouts support canary %s and automatic rollback on eval regressions tied to your golden prompt set.
- Example: internal rollout where canary caught a 12% regression and automatically reverted before user impact.
Demo asset / script: show Evals dashboard with regression alert and the prompt set preview.
Fallback / pilot gating: run a canary with 5% traffic, pre-configured evals. Metric: no >5% QA regression on golden prompts.
Action ask: request the customer golden prompt set (10–25 items) and expected quality metric.
---
Micro-scripts (one-liners sellers can paste into discovery chat):
- Cost-sprint reply: "We usually start with prefix caching + a quantized fallback—can you share a 48h sample traffic export so we can model savings?"
- Latency anchor reply: "We can pin a Dedicated pool for that route and pre-warm your KV cache—what’s your p50/p99 target for interactive flows?"
- Privacy lock reply: "We have a Private deployment path and a checklist for KMS/HSM controls—what regulator or auditor do you need evidence for?"

Open questions / TODOs (field input needed):
- Add one real customer quote per playlet (ask CX for permission).
- Build minimal deck slide set (5 slides) per playlet for quick share.
- Create an interactive Console demo recording for the Cost-Sprint playlet.
- Confirm which internal case studies are shareable (legal).

Quick slide outline (for a 5-slide microdeck that SEs can use live):
1) One-slide signal definition + why it matters to business metrics
2) Our short answer (3 bullets) + 1 callout metric
3) Two proof lines (screenshots or numbers)
4) Demo / how-to steps for the SE to run during call
5) Pilot next steps & success criteria checklist

Next steps (owner + dates):
- Diego: assemble 5-slide shell & Cost-Sprint demo clip (ETA 2026-03-20)
- Li: pull legal-approved excerpts from pilot GM-1987 (ETA 2026-03-18)
- Maya/Omar: run 3 field tests with SEs and capture slack notes (ETA 2026-03-27)

Notes to self / conversational tone guidance for SEs:
- Keep answers outcome-first: "what measurable change can I expect in X weeks" beats product details.
- Use concrete numbers (cost %, latency ms) whenever possible.
- If you’re unsure about shareability, default to "we can provide redacted stats and an architecture diagram."
- Tag feedback in the doc thread with the signal + channel used (e.g., "Cost-Sprint — Slack #pilot-room").

Relevant links (placeholders):
- Quick capacity planner spreadsheet: /sheets/capacity-planner-sample
- Cost case GM-1987 (internal): CONFLUENCE:GM-1987-cost-case
- Private deployment checklist: CONFLUENCE:private-deployment-checklist

End of draft.

Field notes: keep this doc short and iterate. Goal: ship an MVP pack to SEs in 2 weeks and collect usage analytics (which playlets are >3x copied into Slack).
